raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

This PR adds ROCm 7.14 image support for AMD Instinct MI300 (`gfx942`) and MI350 (`gfx950`). It uses AMD's versioned release wheels rather than a nightly channel, so the image remains rebuildable.

The new images use:

- Ubuntu 24.04 and Python 3.12
- ROCm SDK 7.14.0
- PyTorch 2.11.0, torchvision 0.26.0, and torchaudio 2.11.0
- Triton `3.7.1+git0263a6a6`
- AITER `c16d44b`

MI45x / `gfx1250` support is outside this PR and is being developed separately in #32754.

## What changed

- **Docker image:** added a shared ROCm 7.14 base plus `gfx942-rocm714` and `gfx950-rocm714` stages. The base installs the full ROCm development SDK and the device packages required by both architectures; AITER and SGLang kernels are still compiled for the selected GPU only.
- **ROCm SDK compatibility:** ROCm 7.14 installs under the Python environment instead of `/opt/rocm`. The image initializes that SDK and provides the paths and compatibility symlink expected by AITER, MORI, UCX, and the existing Docker build.
- **GPU detection fix:** the pip SDK can expose two copies of `libamd_smi`, causing torch to report zero GPUs even when HIP sees them. The image makes torch and `amdsmi` use the same library.
- **Dependencies:** keeps the ROCm PyTorch packages pinned during later installs, selects the existing PyTorch 2.11-compatible SGLang extras, and exposes the SDK's bundled NUMA/libdrm libraries while rebuilding MORI.
- **CI integration:** teaches `amd_ci_install_dependency.sh` to recognize the two new image flavors and rebuild AITER/MORI with the correct ROCm 7.14 paths.
- **Release workflow:** adds a manual workflow that builds `rocm714-mi30x` and `rocm714-mi35x` images; the nightly schedule remains disabled for now.

Existing ROCm 7.0, 7.2.0, and 7.2.4 image paths keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- Both image variants built successfully: [image build run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563).
- PR and nightly suites were run on both MI30x and MI35x. Compared with nearby ROCm 7.2.0 and 7.2.4 runs, we found **4 new failing test jobs**; all other failures were already present in at least one baseline. See the [run links and per-test comparison](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35319#issuecomment-5367000809).
- The AMD Extra suite passed 3/3. A targeted retry also confirmed that the V4-Pro-MTP resource failure reproduces on ROCm 7.2.4 and is not new to ROCm 7.14.

<!-- pr-states:start -->
---
### CI States

Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #32819241851](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32819241851)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->
Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): <!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:start -->:x: [Run #32819241972](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32819241972)<!-- slot:pr-test-amd-rocm720:end -->

nodes.body:
### ROCm 7.14 validation

Runs: **PR** [MI30x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180) · [MI35x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500988378) | **Nightly** [MI30x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501037209) · [MI35x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501060754)

Compared with the closest available SGLang commits: PR ROCm 7.2.4 `a4ffb99`, PR ROCm 7.2.0 `1df78c2`, and nightly `2ef0fe4`. ROCm 7.14 target: `3b9c66b`.

#### New test regressions

A regression here means that the test passes on both ROCm 7.2.4 and ROCm 7.2.0 baselines, but fails on ROCm 7.14.

| Test | ROCm 7.2.4 | ROCm 7.2.0 | ROCm 7.14 | New failure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| [PR MI30x Stage-A 1GPU-small](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830440544) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | Wave fp16 comparison returns `cosine=NaN` |
| [PR MI30x Stage-B shard 8](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830441367) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | fused-MoE `m=1, top-k=1`: 128/128 outputs are NaN |
| [PR MI30x Stage-B shard 13](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830441436) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | multi-LoRA ROUGE-L `0.977 < 1.0` |
| [Nightly MI35x Grok2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501060754/job/96830587651) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | server warmup sends `image_url` to a text-only model and receives HTTP 400 |

**Total: 4 new failing test jobs.** All other ROCm 7.14 failures were already present in at least one baseline.

Additional checks: [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501007587) passed 3/3. In the [targeted retry](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32515666906), V4-Pro passed, while V4-Pro-MTP reproduced the same out-of-resources failure seen on ROCm 7.2.4.

#### AITER provenance clarification

The validation above used AITER `d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe`, not the current SGLang `main` pin. The linked [image build run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) checked out that commit for both `gfx942` and `gfx950` and published the `20260820` tags. The four PR/nightly runs above actually pulled the `20260821` tags, built by [run 32443714968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32443714968) at `3b9c66b`; that rebuild also checked out the same AITER commit on both architectures.

In all four test runs, `AITER_COMMIT_OVERRIDE` was empty. The dependency logs reported `Dockerfile expects AITER_COMMIT=d9e5ef7...` and image version `v0.1.20.dev12+gd9e5ef7ce`, then explicitly skipped an AITER rebuild. Therefore, these results characterize ROCm 7.14 with AITER `d9e5ef7`; they do not validate the current-main AITER pin `c16d44b93a528b2a4bfd6d8d3409116d465872a9`.

ROCm 7.14 AITER comparison tracking

- current-main `c16d44b93`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32819244956) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32831863435) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32831869250)
- `dc4bdf1c`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32822088835) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32835018294) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32835022817)
- `a6d2b564`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32829676416) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32856262626) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32856269728)

All PR/nightly runs use full matrices, `continue_on_error=true`, and blank `aiter_ref`.

@@ -0,0 +1,113 @@
+name: Release Docker Images Nightly ROCm7.14 (AMD)
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      job_select:
+        description: 'Select which release job to run'
+        required: false
+        type: choice
+        default: 'all'
+        options:
+          - 'all'
+          - publish
+  # Manual dispatch only until the gfx950 leg has been validated on MI355X
+  # hardware; flip this on once both arches have a green run.
+  # schedule:
+  #   - cron: '0 12 * * *'
+
+concurrency:
+  # A PR number if a pull request and otherwise the commit hash. This cancels
+  # queued and in-progress runs for the same PR (presubmit) or commit
+  # (postsubmit). The workflow name is prepended to avoid conflicts between
+  # different workflows.
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.number || github.sha }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  publish:
+    if: github.repository == 'sgl-project/sglang' && (github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.job_select == 'all' || inputs.job_select == 'publish')
+    runs-on: amd-docker-scale
+    environment: 'prod'
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        gpu_arch: ['gfx942-rocm714', 'gfx950-rocm714']
+        build_type: ['all']
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0  # Required for git describe to find tags
+
+      - name: Set up Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: "3.10"
+
+      - name: "Set Date"
+        run: |
+          echo "DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d)" >> $GITHUB_ENV
+
+      - name: Get version from latest tag
+        id: version
+        run: |
+          # Use the shared helper so stable/post releases sort above rc tags.
+          VERSION=$(python3 scripts/release/get_version_tag.py --tag-only | sed 's/^v//')
+
+          if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
+            echo "::error::Could not determine version from git tags"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          # Get short commit hash of current HEAD
+          COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
+
+          # Compose pretend version for setuptools_scm: e.g., 0.5.8.post1.dev20260211+g1a2b3c4
+          PRETEND_VERSION="${VERSION}.dev${{ env.DATE }}+g${COMMIT_HASH}"
+
+          echo "version=${VERSION}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+          echo "pretend_version=${PRETEND_VERSION}" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
+          echo "Detected version: ${VERSION}"
+          echo "Pretend version for pip: ${PRETEND_VERSION}"
+
+      # - name: Login to Docker Hub (AMD)
+      #   uses: docker/login-action@v2
+      #   with:
+      #     username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_AMD_USERNAME }}
+      #     password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_AMD_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Build and Push to rocm/sgl-dev
+        run: |
+          version=${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
+          pretend_version=${{ steps.version.outputs.pretend_version }}
+          echo "Version: ${version}"
+          echo "Pretend version: ${pretend_version}"
+
+          case "${{ matrix.gpu_arch }}" in
+            gfx942-rocm714) rocm_tag="rocm714-mi30x" ;;
+            gfx950-rocm714) rocm_tag="rocm714-mi35x" ;;
+            *)
+              echo "Unsupported gfx arch"
+              exit 1
+              ;;
+          esac
+
+          tag=v${version}-${rocm_tag}
+          echo "IMAGE_TAG=${tag}-${{ env.DATE }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV
+
+          # remove --build-arg NIC_BACKEND=ainic for auto detection nic support in mori
+          # UBUNTU_MIRROR forces apt over HTTPS to dodge port-80 reachability flakes
+          # to Canonical's archive.ubuntu.com mirror IPs from the build runner.
+          docker build . -f docker/rocm.Dockerfile --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=${{ github.sha }} --build-arg BUILD_TYPE=${{ matrix.build_type }} --build-arg GPU_ARCH=${{ matrix.gpu_arch }} --build-arg ENABLE_MORI=1 --build-arg SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=${pretend_version} --build-arg UBUNTU_MIRROR=https://archive.ubuntu.com -t rocm/sgl-dev:${tag}-${{ env.DATE }} --no-cache
+          # docker push rocm/sgl-dev:${tag}-${{ env.DATE }}
+
+      - name: Login to Docker Hub (lmsys)
+        uses: docker/login-action@v2
+        with:
+          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Push to lmsysorg/sglang-rocm
+        run: |
+          docker tag rocm/sgl-dev:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }} lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }}
+          docker push lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:${{ env.IMAGE_TAG }}

@@ -5,11 +5,16 @@
 #   docker build --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=v0.5.10.post1 --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950 -t v0.5.10.post1-rocm700-mi35x -f rocm.Dockerfile .
 #   docker build --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=v0.5.10.post1 --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm720 -t v0.5.10.post1-rocm720-mi35x -f rocm.Dockerfile .
 #   docker build --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=v0.5.10.post1 --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm724 -t v0.5.10.post1-rocm724-mi35x -f rocm.Dockerfile .
+#   docker build --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=v0.5.10.post1 --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx942-rocm714 -t v0.5.10.post1-rocm714-mi30x -f rocm.Dockerfile .
+#   docker build --build-arg SGL_BRANCH=v0.5.10.post1 --build-arg GPU_ARCH=gfx950-rocm714 -t v0.5.10.post1-rocm714-mi35x -f rocm.Dockerfile .
 #
 # Flavor notes:
 #   GPU_ARCH=*-rocm724 is built on a Python 3.12 base and upgrades the stack to
 #   torch 2.11 (+torchvision 0.26 / torchaudio 2.11) and Triton 3.7.
 #   The ROCm 7.2.0 flavors remain on Python 3.10 and torch 2.9.1.
+#   GPU_ARCH=*-rocm714 is Python 3.12 + torch 2.11 as well, but takes the whole
+#   ROCm stack from AMD's pip release channel rather than an apt ROCm base
+#   image; see the rocm714-base stage for what that changes.
 
 # Usage (to build SGLang ROCm + Mori docker image):
 # remove --build-arg NIC_BACKEND=ainic since new MoRI JIT will do NIC auto detection on target
@@ -34,6 +39,11 @@ ARG BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM724="rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_re
 ARG BASE_IMAGE_950="rocm/sgl-dev:rocm7-vllm-20250904"
 ARG BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM720="rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2_ubuntu22.04_py3.10_pytorch_release_2.9.1"
 ARG BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM724="rocm/pytorch:rocm7.2.4_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.10.0"
+# The 7.14 flavors default to the rocm714-base stage below rather than a
+# published image; point these at one to build on a prebuilt base instead.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE_942_ROCM714="rocm714-base"
+ARG BASE_IMAGE_950_ROCM714="rocm714-base"
+ARG BASE_IMAGE_ROCM714="ubuntu:24.04"
 
 # This is necessary for scope purpose
 ARG GPU_ARCH=gfx950
@@ -126,6 +136,140 @@ RUN mkdir -p /etc/sglang/constraints && : > /etc/sglang/constraints/torch-rocm.t
 # IPC behavior.
 ENV HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1
 
+# ===============================
+# Shared ROCm 7.14 base for gfx942 and gfx950. ROCm 7.14 is published as pip
+# wheels and docker images only -- repo.radeon.com has no apt repo for it -- and
+# no rocm/pytorch tag carries the arch set we want, so the stack is assembled
+# from AMD's ROCm pip release channel on a plain Ubuntu base. That puts the SDK
+# in site-packages instead of /opt/rocm, which the rest of this Dockerfile and
+# AITER both assume, hence the path fixups at the end of this stage.
+#
+# repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch is the release index (it also mirrors the
+# PyPI deps torch pulls in, so one --index-url is enough). Deliberately not the
+# nightly or devrelease channels: those get pruned, which would leave this
+# Dockerfile unbuildable once the pinned build ages out.
+#
+# Python 3.12 (the Ubuntu 24.04 default) rather than 3.13/3.14: st_attn==0.0.7,
+# vsa==0.0.4, petit_kernel==0.0.2 and wave-lang==3.8.2 publish wheels only up to
+# cp313 and no sdist, so pip has no candidate at all for srt_hip on 3.14.
+FROM $BASE_IMAGE_ROCM714 AS rocm714-base
+
+# ROCM_TRITON_VERSION rather than TRITON_VERSION: the final stage declares a
+# TRITON_VERSION of its own for the ROCm 7.2 wheel, and a --build-arg would
+# otherwise land on both.
+ARG ROCM_VERSION="7.14.0"
+ARG ROCM_TORCH_VERSION="2.11.0"
+ARG ROCM_TORCHVISION_VERSION="0.26.0"
+ARG ROCM_TRITON_VERSION="3.7.1+git0263a6a6"
+ARG ROCM_INDEX_URL="https://repo.amd.com/rocm/whl-multi-arch/"
+
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+        build-essential \
+        ca-certificates \
+        curl \
+        git \
+        gnupg \
+        libstdc++-12-dev \
+        python-is-python3 \
+        python3 \
+        python3-dev \
+        python3-pip \
+        python3.12-venv \
+        wget \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+ENV VIRTUAL_ENV=/opt/venv
+RUN python3 -m venv "$VIRTUAL_ENV"
+ENV PATH="$VIRTUAL_ENV/bin:$PATH"
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir -U pip setuptools setuptools_scm wheel
+
+# Both arches' device wheels go into the shared base; GPU_ARCH_LIST still
+# narrows what AITER and sgl-kernel actually compile for per stage. The device
+# wheels are named as their own specs rather than as extras, because several
+# device extras in one spec (torch[device-gfx942,device-gfx950]) silently
+# installs only the first and the missing arch then fails at runtime with
+# hipErrorInvalidImage.
+RUN python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir \
+        --index-url ${ROCM_INDEX_URL} \
+        "rocm-sdk-core==${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "rocm-sdk-libraries==${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "rocm-sdk-devel==${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "rocm-sdk-device-gfx942==${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "rocm-sdk-device-gfx950==${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "torch==${ROCM_TORCH_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "torchvision==${ROCM_TORCHVISION_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "torchaudio==${ROCM_TORCH_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "amd-torch-device-gfx942==${ROCM_TORCH_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "amd-torch-device-gfx950==${ROCM_TORCH_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "amd-torchvision-device-gfx942==${ROCM_TORCHVISION_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "amd-torchvision-device-gfx950==${ROCM_TORCHVISION_VERSION}+rocm${ROCM_VERSION}" \
+        "triton==${ROCM_TRITON_VERSION}.rocm${ROCM_VERSION}"
+
+RUN rocm-sdk init && rocm-sdk targets
+
+# rocm-sdk init expands a devel tree that carries its own copy of libamd_smi,
+# byte-identical to the one in _rocm_sdk_core that HIP loads through its RPATH.
+# Since ROCM_HOME below puts the devel tree on LD_LIBRARY_PATH, the amdsmi
+# python package binds that second copy while torch already holds the first,
+# and two independent copies in one process each keep their own global state:
+# whichever initialises second enumerates no devices. torch asks amdsmi for the
+# device count before HIP, so `torch.cuda.device_count()` comes back 0 on a
+# machine where hipGetDeviceCount() says 1. Collapse the duplicate so both land
+# on the same library. Idempotent when the SDK already ships a symlink here.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    SP="$VIRTUAL_ENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages"; \
+    CORE=$(ls "$SP"/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/libamd_smi.so.* 2>/dev/null | head -1); \
+    DEVEL="$SP/_rocm_sdk_devel/lib/libamd_smi.so"; \
+    if [ -n "${CORE}" ] && [ -e "${DEVEL}" ] && [ ! -L "${DEVEL}" ]; then \
+      ln -sf "${CORE}" "${DEVEL}"; \
+      echo "linked ${DEVEL} -> ${CORE}"; \
+    fi
+
+ENV ROCM_HOME=$VIRTUAL_ENV/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_devel
+ENV ROCM_PATH=$ROCM_HOME
+ENV CPATH=$ROCM_HOME/include
+ENV LIBRARY_PATH=$ROCM_HOME/lib
+ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$ROCM_HOME/lib
+RUN echo 'export PATH=$ROCM_HOME/llvm/bin:$ROCM_HOME/bin:$PATH' >> /etc/bash.bashrc
+
+# The SDK's hsakmtTargets.cmake hardcodes /usr/lib64/libc.so from its own build
+# host; Ubuntu keeps libc in /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, so cmake would otherwise
+# fail with "ninja: error: /usr/lib64/libc.so missing and no known rule to make it".

### ROCm 7.14 validation

Runs: **PR** [MI30x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180) · [MI35x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500988378) | **Nightly** [MI30x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501037209) · [MI35x](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501060754)

Compared with the closest available SGLang commits: PR ROCm 7.2.4 `a4ffb99`, PR ROCm 7.2.0 `1df78c2`, and nightly `2ef0fe4`. ROCm 7.14 target: `3b9c66b`.

#### New test regressions

A regression here means that the test passes on both ROCm 7.2.4 and ROCm 7.2.0 baselines, but fails on ROCm 7.14.

| Test | ROCm 7.2.4 | ROCm 7.2.0 | ROCm 7.14 | New failure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| [PR MI30x Stage-A 1GPU-small](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830440544) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | Wave fp16 comparison returns `cosine=NaN` |
| [PR MI30x Stage-B shard 8](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830441367) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | fused-MoE `m=1, top-k=1`: 128/128 outputs are NaN |
| [PR MI30x Stage-B shard 13](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32500976180/job/96830441436) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | multi-LoRA ROUGE-L `0.977 < 1.0` |
| [Nightly MI35x Grok2](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501060754/job/96830587651) | Pass | Pass | **Fail** | server warmup sends `image_url` to a text-only model and receives HTTP 400 |

**Total: 4 new failing test jobs.** All other ROCm 7.14 failures were already present in at least one baseline.

Additional checks: [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32501007587) passed 3/3. In the [targeted retry](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32515666906), V4-Pro passed, while V4-Pro-MTP reproduced the same out-of-resources failure seen on ROCm 7.2.4.

#### AITER provenance clarification

The validation above used AITER `d9e5ef7ce08ee7045d583aed768cff41aa9210fe`, not the current SGLang `main` pin. The linked [image build run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32380153563) checked out that commit for both `gfx942` and `gfx950` and published the `20260820` tags. The four PR/nightly runs above actually pulled the `20260821` tags, built by [run 32443714968](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32443714968) at `3b9c66b`; that rebuild also checked out the same AITER commit on both architectures.

In all four test runs, `AITER_COMMIT_OVERRIDE` was empty. The dependency logs reported `Dockerfile expects AITER_COMMIT=d9e5ef7...` and image version `v0.1.20.dev12+gd9e5ef7ce`, then explicitly skipped an AITER rebuild. Therefore, these results characterize ROCm 7.14 with AITER `d9e5ef7`; they do not validate the current-main AITER pin `c16d44b93a528b2a4bfd6d8d3409116d465872a9`.

ROCm 7.14 AITER comparison tracking

- current-main `c16d44b93`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32819244956) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32831863435) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32831869250)
- `dc4bdf1c`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32822088835) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32835018294) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32835022817)
- `a6d2b564`: [release](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32829676416) ✅ · [PR full](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32856262626) · [nightly](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32856269728)

All PR/nightly runs use full matrices, `continue_on_error=true`, and blank `aiter_ref`.
